analysis_status: post-identifiability observation-model robustness stress test; not a latent ecological effect analysis

ecological_read.supported: Allowing extra-binomial heterogeneity in repeated focal-interaction detections materially changes the observation model in every primary transition.
ecological_read.model_comparison: The beta-binomial detection model has AIC at least 13.8 lower than the simple binomial model in every transition, and much larger improvements in four transitions.
ecological_read.state_instability: At least one latent transition parameter is driven to the frozen logit boundary in all six transitions under the richer detection model.
ecological_read.consequence: The simple-binomial latent gain/loss estimates are not robust enough to restore a detection-corrected ecological rewiring response.

not_established: the beta-binomial model is the true observation process
true latent gain or loss rates
the biological fraction of the 853 raw observed-link changes
claim_ceiling: Observation-model sensitivity is decisive under the frozen stress rule: beta-binomial detection is preferred in 6/6 transitions and latent transition estimates hit a state boundary in 6/6. Detection-corrected rewiring therefore remains model-dependent and must not be promoted as an identified ecological response.
